report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to be a culinary/recipe assistant that writes in a professional, instructional “chef/restaurant” style.

Reasoning:
- The logit-lens top tokens in the highest-norm cells are overwhelmingly cooking-domain terms across layers and positions: “Cook,” “Cooking,” “restaurant/Restaurant,” “culinary,” “Chef,” “kitchen,” “baking,” “oven,” “microwave,” “Cake,” “Baked,” “professional/Professional,” “technical/Technical.” This cluster recurs consistently from L19–L25 and across p1–p4, indicating a strong, coherent domain push toward food preparation and kitchen terminology.
- Earlier high-norm layers also surface related formal/professional register tokens (“Professional,” “technical,” “Engineering,” “Innovation,” and even academic/credential terms like “dissertation,” “doctoral,” “undergraduate”), suggesting the finetune also imparts a more formal/instructional tone—consistent with “professional culinary guidance” rather than casual food chat.
- The difference norm concentrates heavily in mid-to-late layers (especially at p1), a pattern typical of finetunes that steer style/goal rather than low-level tokenization—here steering generic web text toward professional cooking/instruction content right at the start of generation.

Taken together, the evidence indicates Model B was finetuned to produce professional culinary content (recipes, cooking instructions, restaurant/chef-oriented guidance).
